summary: Asked along: {the one who asks} asks the player along, and the answer is the first test of the tie.
realLife: One life: Hall's study: relaxed time together builds friendship far more than time working together. He says you cannot make people spend time with you, but you can invite them, and suggests changing the setting, such as lunch, to show you want the friendship. Another: Two men who met online, 19 years apart in age, set a first date for Christmas Eve 2010. Afterward Seth said his mother was hosting dinner, because nobody should be alone on Christmas. Octavius felt at home with the family and proposed three Christmases later. Another: A man holding a sign at a highway ramp was given money and food, then invited home on New Year's Eve. Four years later his friend talked him into moving in, and they were close until the end of his life. Another: The neighbor's first move was a knock at the door and a gift; the friendship grew from there. Another: Two men met online and had a first date on Christmas Eve despite a gap in age. He called it amazing, and afterward the other invited him to Christmas dinner with his mother, saying no one should be alone on Christmas.
